name: Search box
purpose: Lets the user type what they're looking for where they are and search for it, on a card of its own with a search button, such as a vehicle's registration to check its tax and MOT. A hint of what to type, such as a blank number plate, can sit inside it.

proposed.design: a screenshot of the future driving designs in Figma, until there’s a link to the file

origin.notes: From the future driving designs, under Check a vehicle. It looks as the app's vehicle search does today (VehicleCheckSectionView): a card with a blank plate reading ABC and SF's magnifyingglass on a primaryBlue circle. But that's a button, which opens a panel above the keyboard to type the registration in (VehicleCheckCoordinator, RegistrationNumberField); in the designs, the user types in the box itself. For a search bar in the system's own style, such as the home screen's, use the search field.

placeholder.description: What the box shows until the user types, such as Start, as the designs have it, or Search for a vehicle.

label.description: The box's name for screen readers, such as Registration number. Without it, they hear its placeholder.

name.description: The name what the user typed is sent as.

action.description: Where the search goes, such as the page of results. Without it, the page it's on.

inputs.content: Optionally, an element with slot="accessory", inside the box after the text, hinting at what to type, such as <govuk-app-number-plate variant="front">ABC</govuk-app-number-plate>. Screen readers don't hear it.

events.name: submit
events.description: From its form, when the user presses its search button or Search on the keyboard.

events.name: input
events.description: From its box, as the user types.

rules: Put it in a section that says what it searches for, such as Check a vehicle, with a description, such as View information for any vehicle.
Give it a label saying what to type, such as Registration number, when its placeholder doesn't: screen readers don't hear its accessory.
Give it an accessory only where it shows what to type, as a blank number plate does for a registration.
For a search bar in the system's style, such as at the top of a screen or a list, use the search field.

avoid.when: To search GOV.UK, or filter a list, such as of countries
To ask a question on a form, with a button below to carry on

ios.symbol: button, the vehicle search it looks like
RegistrationNumberField, where the app has the user type a registration today

references.description: The app's vehicle search, a button it looks like, in light mode

examples.name: A vehicle's registration, with a blank number plate
examples.html:
<govuk-app-section title="Check a vehicle" description="View information for any vehicle">
  <govuk-app-search-box placeholder="Start" label="Registration number" name="registration" action="#vehicle">
    <govuk-app-number-plate slot="accessory" variant="front">ABC</govuk-app-number-plate>
  </govuk-app-search-box>
</govuk-app-section>

examples.name: Without an accessory
examples.html:
<govuk-app-section title="Find your local council" description="Check which council looks after where you live">
  <govuk-app-search-box placeholder="Postcode" name="postcode" action="#council"></govuk-app-search-box>
</govuk-app-section>
